exposure: Major earthquake experienced during the first trimester of pregnancy
cohort: The participants were women with singleton pregnancies, categorized into a post-earthquake cohort (pregnant during the 2011 Christchurch earthquake in their first trimester) and a pre-earthquake cohort (pregnant in 2009).
finding: The study found no significant difference in the rate of preterm birth between women who experienced a major earthquake in their first trimester and those who did not.
